seal.statement: The CDC group propagation service admits every durable wave its source lane presents: no wave is refused, delayed or ordered because another lane's wave is in flight. The node-wide propagation slot and every mechanism that existed to share it (per-table slice counts, the yield hold, the waiting-table queue with its lifecycles and timestamps, credits, the slice-turn wake, contention marks on the invocation, and the lane-side contention registration, release and hint handling) are removed from source, tests and documentation, not disabled. In-flight waves are bounded structurally by one per source lane; stopping the service retires every in-flight wave and arms nothing; after a refusal that attempted nothing the lane composes its next vector from the current owed tail. Coverage, receipts, acknowledgement, order within a lane and every timeout, retry count and bound value are unchanged.

Transition record, scope and draft coverage model before any edit (base 589c1e2f, rule-set revision 5; lead plans, one writer, separate verifier). Sources: journey measurement of 2026-11-14 (evidence/receipt.json); history of the sender retained at lagrange-foundation-coordination-20261114/history-cdc-sender.md; design note cdc-delivery-design-note-2026-11-11.md section 5.3 part 2b and 5.5 (direction only; its code is not imported); comparable systems (no system studied serialises independent ordered streams through one node-wide lock: order per stream, bound per destination by a window, wake on completion).
1 Producer/consumer symbols: producer = the partition lane's subscriber call into buildPartitionCdcPropagationSubscriber -> propagatePartitionCDCEvent -> CDCGroupPropagationService.propagateCDCEvent -> propagateDurableCdcEvent (src/topology/cdc-group-propagation-durable-delivery.js). Removed there: DURABLE_PROPAGATION_ADMISSION.BUSY and the admission against owner.activeDurablePropagation; CONTENDED_TABLE_SLICE_WAVES, CONTENDED_SLICE_YIELD_HOLD_MS, BUSY_CONTENDED_RETRY_AFTER_MS, MIN_YIELD_HOLD_RETRY_AFTER_MS; the waiting-table queue, timestamps, lifecycles, credits, the yield hold, notifyNextWaitingDurableSliceTable, advance/finish slice bookkeeping, releaseWaitingDurableSliceContender; in the service: the slice fields and releaseDurableSliceContender; in the lane (src/partition): registerLaneContentionOwner, releaseContendedPropagationOwners and lane.contendedPropagationOwners, wakeContendedLaneForSliceTurn, lane.sliceTurnReady and its retry-hint consumption, the contention-driven page yield; on the delivery invocation (src/cdc/cdc-delivery-invocation.js): markContended, isContended, registerContentionOwner. Consumers to census: every reader of those fields (diagnostics, admin, readiness, stats, tests, docs, src/topology/INDEX.md).
2 Shape: unchanged request (events vector, delivery invocation, source message group) and unchanged answer (committed / provisional / unknown outcome). The only removed outcome is the slot's BACKPRESSURE refusal; typed backpressure from the pressure governor and from a recipient's commit queue remains.
3 Identity/generation: a wave belongs to (propagation lifetime, source lane invocation, source group). Unchanged.
4 Ordering: per lane, one vector in flight, vectors in ledger order (the lane's single flight). Across lanes none, as the architecture already states (delivery has no global ordering; the cache apply is order-insensitive).
5 Absent vs unavailable: stopped service -> typed unknown with reason propagation_stopped; source group mismatch -> typed unknown with its reason; pressure governor defer and recipient queue full -> typed backpressure. No 'busy'.
6 Durable commit: unchanged (recipient group commit makes the receipt; CDC_DELIVERED in the source partition makes rows delivered).
7 Retained obligations: an uncovered vector stays owed in its lane's ledger exactly as today; the service holds no payload between attempts and now holds only the set of in-flight waves, each owned by its invocation and released by actual child cleanup.
8 Wake and cleanup: no slot-release wake exists because nothing waits for a slot; lane wakes are the existing ones (committed entry, leader elected, handshake, retry timer, after flush). Stop retires every in-flight wave; a retired wave's lane keeps its debt.
Added behaviour in the lane (the one non-deletion): after a refusal or hold that attempted nothing and with no leaf coverage in the progress cell, the next composition re-captures the owed tail instead of reusing the tail captured when the earlier pass began (measured: 742 drives cut at a stale tail with 1-10 READY rows behind it).
Writable paths: src/topology/cdc-group-propagation-durable-delivery.js, cdc-group-propagation-service.js, cdc-group-propagation-lifecycle-methods.js, cdc-group-propagation-constants.js, src/topology/INDEX.md; src/partition/partition-cdc-obligation-delivery.js, -lane.js, -progress.js, -range.js; src/cdc/cdc-delivery-invocation.js; any reader of the removed fields found by the census; the tests that pin the slot and slices (the seven 'contended durable propagation' cases and every file referencing the removed symbols) and new reproducers. Excluded: message-group files, cache, ledger, recipient cursors, re-list, any timeout or bound value, journey predicates.
DRAFT COVERAGE MODEL (to be challenged before evidence is written). Claim: for any set of source lanes with owed vectors and any schedule of leaf answers, (i) a wave is admitted when its lane presents it unless a typed non-slot outcome applies; (ii) the time for lane A's vector to reach its recipients does not depend on whether lane B's wave settles, up to a shared recipient's own typed backpressure; (iii) per-lane order, coverage and acknowledgement are exactly as before; (iv) at most one in-flight wave per lane and no state grows with the number of refused or waiting lanes; (v) stop retires every in-flight wave and arms nothing; (vi) no removed symbol survives. Decisions: admit; capture plan; deliver leaves; foreground retry; finish and release; stop. State: number of lanes with owed work (1, two partitions of one table, two tables, many); waves in flight per source group; a wave awaiting its source apply / a target / a foreground retry sleep / child cleanup after finish; service state (created, initialized, running, stopped, restarted with a new lifetime); propagation mode (grouped, safe) and its change mid-wave; recipient set growing or a route replaced mid-wave; pressure governor defer. Events: leaf answers committed, provisional, unknown, backpressure, throw, never settling; a lane's tenure change or shutdown while its wave is in flight; service stop with several waves in flight; the same lane presenting again after its wave finished but before child cleanup; two lanes of one table. Temporal: admission; between admission and plan capture; while a leaf is awaited; in a retry sleep; after finish before cleanup; after stop. Outputs: admissions and their absence of refusal; per-lane delivery times; coverage and acknowledgement; stats and publication-mode diagnostics; emitted propagated events; lane retry dispositions and delays; memory held per wave and in total. Evidence: isolation reproducers at zero virtual time (a never-settling wave of one lane does not hold another lane's vector), a many-lane run with all waves overlapping, stop with several in flight, the removed-mechanism census, the tail re-capture witness, a differential against the base for a single lane (identical outcomes when there is nothing to contend with), and a guard-versus-mutation table.

Phase A (no src change). 7f0c1016e: mechanical regeneration of test class registries + import-graph seal (base 589c1e2f left the lifecycle candidate's system-table-cache-lifecycle-reconciliation-differential.test.js unclassified: 2665 vs 2666; seal stale). 4cc448949: reproducers to the slot-free behaviour: test/topology/cdc-group-propagation-wave-isolation.test.js (R1 cross-table isolation at zero virtual time, R2 cross-partition isolation, R3 eight lanes in one turn all in flight, R5 stop with three waves in flight retires every invocation and arms nothing, R6b no per-lane collection retained), test/partition/partition-cdc-lane-wave-isolation.test.js (R4 presenting lane drains with no retry timer/hint, R6a per-lane single flight [invariant], R8 single-lane differential x2 [must stay green]), test/partition/partition-cdc-obligation-scan-recapture.test.js (R7 owed tail re-captured after owner-not-ready refusal); harness createHeldMessageRouter/beginDurableCdcInvocation/sourcePartition, fixture multiLaneTopologyFixture. MODEL AMENDMENT after the hidden-serialisation challenge (2026-11-14, by the lead). Source: lagrange-foundation-coordination-20261114/slot-removal/challenge-hidden-serialization.md (A1-A10, B1-B5, worst-case table), read from the code at 7d6cdbfaa. It amends the transition record and the draft model of this quest; where they differ this entry governs. The sealed text is not edited.

CORRECTIONS TO THE TRANSITION RECORD.
C-1 (A1) Item 5 was wrong. The slot's busy answer was the only typed backpressure a lane ever received from the propagation subscriber. Any other uncovered leaf (pressure-governor defer, a recipient commit queue at capacity, a router rejection or preemption) ends the wave as a plain unknown with no reason and no hint, because the wave's aggregate answer drops the leaf's own typed answer. The lane then treats it as a transient failure: it halves its shipping window, backs off up to its transient maximum and logs at warn. With the slot gone these answers become the lane's normal experience of pressure, so the repair must carry them truthfully: when every leaf left uncovered by a wave was refused by typed backpressure before any effect at that leaf, the wave's answer is typed backpressure carrying the smallest hint the leaves gave; a wave with any other uncovered leaf stays unknown. The lane's existing backpressure handling (window unchanged, hinted delay) then applies. No delay or bound value changes.
C-2 (A2) Claim (ii) was false as worded. The message router is a shared, bounded resource per destination node (a bounded number in flight, bounded pending per class, a per-table cap, and preemption of a pending delivery by a critical-table delivery), and each leaf can hold its place for the delivery timeout. Replacement for (ii): the propagation service adds no dependency between lanes; a lane's vector can be delayed by another lane only through a recipient-side or transport-side bound that answers with typed backpressure, never by waiting for another lane's wave to finish. Isolation reproducers must stay inside the router's per-destination and per-table bounds, and one reproducer must exceed them and show typed backpressure reaching the lane.
C-3 (A8) A pressure-governor defer is evaluated per target leaf after the source leaf may already have committed, so it is not 'attempted nothing' for the vector: the cell holds source coverage, the identical vector is re-presented (pinning) and only the deferred leaves are retried. The tail re-capture applies only when the progress cell holds no leaf coverage.

ADDED TO THE REPAIR (inside the same interaction).
R-1 (A3) Stop, initialize and a lifetime change retire every in-flight wave, not one; the service owns the set of in-flight waves for exactly that purpose; a wave of an old lifetime produces no further effect; nothing is armed after stop with any number of waves in flight or asleep in a foreground retry.
R-2 (A4) Publication mode is node-wide and last-writer-wins and feeds the readiness decision guard. Overlapping waves must not flap it: setting the mode a wave's plan implies is a no-op when it equals the current mode and records no transition; a witness drives overlapping waves with the same plan and asserts zero transitions. If two waves on one node can legitimately plan different modes (different source groups), that case is pinned by a test and reported, not resolved by guessing.
R-3 (A6) The 'foreground retry spent' report is emitted once per wave, unthrottled and persisted, so with many lanes failing together it can feed the logs table's own lane. It takes the same console-only, throttled route its sibling report already uses, in the same owner file.
R-4 The lane-side tail re-capture as recorded, restricted by C-3.

NOT BUILT HERE, DECIDED BY MEASUREMENT (constraint structural-bound-replaces-the-slot stays in force; the challenge showed 'no node-wide limiter is needed' is not defensible from the code alone).
M-1 (A5) Each wave captures the routing plan many times (a cache scan per currentness check) and the governor scans outbound queues per target leaf; with the slot the node ran about three waves per second, without it nothing caps the rate of overlapping waves except the lanes themselves.
M-2 (A7) A source-group leader change fails every in-flight wave at once and lane retry delays carry no jitter.
M-3 (A9) Memory is bounded only structurally: lanes x vector bytes x the copies made per leaf.
The candidate's journey run must therefore record, and the lead decides from the numbers whether a bounded window is needed as the next unit: peak concurrent waves; event-loop delay and its maximum on every node; router rejections and preemptions per destination for CDC and for other traffic; the source group's commit-waiter peak; resident memory; commit-to-arrival latency per table; count of persisted error rows from propagation; lane retry counts by disposition.

MODEL ROWS ADDED (A10). Decisions: the wave's aggregate answer (committed, provisional, typed backpressure, unknown); publication-mode write; in-flight set add and remove; retire-all. State: number of overlapping waves per destination against the router's bounds (below, at, above); per-table router cap; delivery class of the table (critical, background); waves asleep in a foreground retry; source groups per node (one, several). Events: router rejection; router preemption of a pending delivery; recipient commit queue full; governor defer on the first target after the source leaf committed; source-group leader change with N waves in flight; stop, initialize and restart with N waves in flight; the logs table as a source lane. Temporal: between the source leaf's commit and a deferred target; between stop and the settlement of a delivery already on the wire. Outputs: the typed reason and hint the lane receives; the lane's window after each answer; publication-mode transitions; persisted log rows; the in-flight set's size after every path (must return to zero).
